tgt: Nama, asal, umur, pekerjaan, hobi: naskah untuk pertemuan pertama.

tgt: Minta bantuan, minta diulang, membayar, menemukan jalan lagi.

tgt: Toilet, pintu keluar, tempat duduk, wifi, jam buka: semua pertanyaan "di mana".

src: Sizes, hot/iced, points cards, heating food, bags.
tgt: Ukuran, panas atau dingin, kartu poin, menghangatkan makanan, kantong plastik.

tgt: Hidangan dan bahan yang ada di setiap menu.

tgt: 12 kata kerja yang kamu pakai setiap hari, dalam bentuk sopan.

tgt: Bilangan asli Korea dan bilangan Sino-Korea, dan kapan memakai masing-masing.

tgt: Imut, cantik, kangen: untuk orang yang dekat denganmu.

src: Getting a number, asking out, saying how you feel.

tgt: Mengajak, menentukan tempat dan waktu, lalu pamit.

tgt: Kosakata fandom dari 최애 sampai 떼창.

tgt: Kabar terbaru, cuaca, rencana akhir pekan, cara pamit yang benar.

tgt: Memesan, kata penggolong untuk makanan, dua ungkapan saat makan.
Kiri, kanan, lurus; kereta bawah tanah, bus, taksi.

tgt: Hari ini, besok, nama-nama hari, jam berapa sekarang.

tgt: Reaksi dan kalimat yang kamu dengar di setiap episode.

src: Vertical stroke, tick to the right.
tgt: Garis tegak, dengan garis kecil ke kanan.
eo: satu vokal, dari e pada "enam" dengan mulut lebih terbuka
Garis kecil ke kiri. Bukan o: bibir tidak bulat.
o seperti pada "toko", bibir lebih bulat
Garis mendatar, garis kecil ke atas.
Garis mendatar, garis kecil ke bawah.

src: like the vowel in 'book' with lips flat
tgt: eu: satu vokal, u dengan bibir datar
rw: English sound comparison ("like the x in …")

src: No English match; smile and say 'oo'.
tgt: Tidak ada dalam bahasa Indonesia: ucapkan u sambil tersenyum (mirip eu dalam bahasa Sunda).

src: e as in bed (open; same sound as ㅔ today)
tgt: e seperti pada "sate" (kini sama dengan ㅔ)

src: Modern Korean: sounds same as ㅔ.
tgt: Dalam bahasa Korea modern, bunyinya sama dengan ㅔ.

src: Same sound as ㅐ in speech.
tgt: Saat diucapkan, bunyinya sama dengan ㅐ.

src: ㅏ with an extra tick = y-glide.
tgt: ㅏ dengan satu garis tambahan = ada bunyi y di depannya.
yeo: y + eo, satu suku kata

src: g (soft) at start, k at syllable end
tgt: g ringan di awal, k di akhir suku kata
가 = ga, 악 = ak (k akhir ini bukan hentian seperti pada "tidak").

src: d at start, t at end
tgt: d di awal, t di akhir

src: flap r between vowels, l at end
tgt: r satu ketukan di antara vokal, l di akhir
라 = ra, 물 = mul. r-nya tidak digetarkan.

src: b at start, p at end
tgt: b di awal, p di akhir

src: silent at start, ng at end
tgt: tidak berbunyi di awal, ng di akhir
아 = a, 강 = gang (ng seperti pada "datang").
ch: c pada "cari" dengan embusan (ㅈ berembus)

src: 까 kka. Tight throat, no air. 꽃 = flower, 까만 = black.
tgt: 까 kka. Tenggorokan dikencangkan, tanpa embusan. 꽃 = bunga, 까만 = hitam.

src: 따 tta. 딸 = daughter, 똑바로 = straight.
tgt: 따 tta. 딸 = anak perempuan, 똑바로 = lurus.

src: 빠 ppa. 빨리 = quickly, 아빠 = dad.
tgt: 빠 ppa. 빨리 = cepat, 아빠 = ayah.

src: 싸 ssa. 쌀 = rice, 있어요 = there is.
tgt: 싸 ssa. 쌀 = beras, 있어요 = ada.

src: 짜 jja. 짜다 = salty, 진짜 = really.
tgt: 짜 jja. 짜다 = asin, 진짜 = sungguh.

src: ㅗ + ㅏ. 과일 = fruit, 와요 = come.
tgt: ㅗ + ㅏ. 과일 = buah, 와요 = datang.

src: ㅜ + ㅓ. 원 = won, 뭐 = what.
tgt: ㅜ + ㅓ. 원 = won, 뭐 = apa.

src: ㅗ + ㅣ. 회사 = company, 외국 = foreign country.
tgt: ㅗ + ㅣ. 회사 = perusahaan, 외국 = luar negeri.

src: ㅜ + ㅣ. 귀 = ear, 위 = up / stomach.
tgt: ㅜ + ㅣ. 귀 = telinga, 위 = atas / lambung.

src: Both sound like 'we'. 왜 = why, 웨딩 = wedding.
tgt: Keduanya dibaca "we". 왜 = kenapa, 웨딩 = pernikahan.

src: 의사 = doctor (ui), 거의 = almost (i), 친구의 = friend's (e).
tgt: 의사 = dokter (ui), 거의 = hampir (i), 친구의 = milik teman (e).
Keduanya dibaca "ye". 얘기 = obrolan / cerita, 예 = ya (formal).

src: all sound like t at the end
tgt: semuanya dibaca t di akhir, tanpa dilepas

src: 옷 ot, 있다 itda, 꽃 kkot, 끝 kkeut, 낮 nat.
tgt: 옷 ot, 있다 itda, 꽃 kkot, 끝 kkeut, 낮 nat.
부엌 bueok (dapur), 밖 bak (luar). Pangkal lidah menempel, bukan hentian seperti pada "tidak".

src: Only one sounds: 닭 dak (chicken), 값 gap (price), 읽다 ikda.
tgt: Hanya satu yang berbunyi: 닭 dak (ayam), 값 gap (harga), 읽다 ikda.

src: Only 7 sounds survive at the end of a syllable: k, n, t, l, m, p, ng. 옷 sounds like 'ot', 꽃 like 'kkot'.
tgt: Di akhir suku kata hanya ada 7 bunyi: k, n, t, l, m, p, ng. 옷 dibaca "ot" dan 꽃 dibaca "kkot", tanpa dilepas, seperti akhir "sakit".

src: 살 (sal, flesh) vs 쌀 (ssal, rice). Tense = tighter throat, no air puff.
tgt: 살 (sal, daging) vs 쌀 (ssal, beras). Tegang = tenggorokan lebih kencang, tanpa embusan.

src: g · kk · k (k-row: plain, tense, aspirated)
tgt: g · kk · k (deret k: dasar, tegang, berembus)

src: 가 ga / 까 kka / 카 ka. Aspirated = big puff of air; tense = none, tight.
tgt: 가 ga / 까 kka / 카 ka. Berembus = ada angin keluar; tegang = tanpa angin dan kencang, mirip k Indonesia.

src: d · tt · t (t-row: plain, tense, aspirated)
tgt: d · tt · t (deret t: dasar, tegang, berembus)

src: 달 dal (moon) / 딸 ttal (daughter) / 탈 tal (mask).
tgt: 달 dal (bulan) / 딸 ttal (anak perempuan) / 탈 tal (topeng).

src: b · pp · p (p-row: plain, tense, aspirated)
tgt: b · pp · p (deret p: dasar, tegang, berembus)

src: 불 bul (fire) / 뿔 ppul (horn) / 풀 pul (grass).
tgt: 불 bul (api) / 뿔 ppul (tanduk) / 풀 pul (rumput).

src: j · jj · ch (ch-row: plain, tense, aspirated)
tgt: j · jj · ch (deret ch: dasar, tegang, berembus)

src: 자다 jada (sleep) / 짜다 jjada (salty) / 차다 chada (cold).
tgt: 자다 jada (tidur) / 짜다 jjada (asin) / 차다 chada (dingin saat disentuh).

src: A final consonant jumps to the next vowel: 한국어 → 한구거 (han-gu-geo), 음악 → 으막 (eu-mak).
tgt: Konsonan akhir pindah ke vokal berikutnya, tanpa hentian: 한국어 → 한구거 (han-gu-geo), 음악 → 으막 (eu-mak).

src: 머리 meori, 다리 dari. At the end: l sound, 물 mul.
tgt: 머리 meori, 다리 dari. Di akhir dibaca l: 물 mul.
빨리 ppalli (cepat), 몰라 molla. l-nya ditahan, bukan r.
ㅎ hampir hilang di antara vokal
좋아요 → 조아요 (joayo). 많이 → 마니 (mani). Seperti "lihat" yang menjadi "liat".

src: 강 gang, 사랑 sarang. Never 'n-g' separated.
tgt: 강 gang, 사랑 sarang. Satu bunyi, bukan n lalu g.

src: ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ before ㄴ/ㅁ turn nasal: 감사합니다 → 감사함니다, 국물 → 궁물.
tgt: ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ sebelum ㄴ/ㅁ menjadi bunyi sengau: 감사합니다 → 감사함니다, 국물 → 궁물.

src: 의사 ui-sa (doctor) at the start; 거의 geo-i; possessive 의 → 에 (친구의 → 친구에).
tgt: 의사 ui-sa (dokter) di awal kata; 거의 geo-i; 의 penanda milik → 에 (친구의 → 친구에).
bunyinya sama dalam bahasa Seoul sekarang

src: 개 and 게 sound identical; context decides.
tgt: 개 dan 게 terdengar sama; konteks yang menentukan.
eo dan o: dua vokal yang berbeda

src: ㅓ = jaw open, lips relaxed (uh). ㅗ = lips round (oh). 서울 vs 소울.
tgt: ㅓ = mulut terbuka, bibir tidak bulat, berangkat dari e pada "enam". ㅗ = bibir bulat, seperti o pada "toko". 서울 vs 소울.

src: No English match. Say 'oo' while smiling. 음, 그, 는.
tgt: Tidak ada dalam bahasa Indonesia. Ucapkan u sambil tersenyum. 음, 그, 는.

src: 가요↗ = are you going? 가요↘ = I'm going. Same word.
tgt: 가요↗ = kamu mau pergi? 가요↘ = saya pergi. Katanya sama, seperti dalam bahasa Indonesia lisan.

src: 저는 밥을 먹어요: 저는 / 밥을 / 먹어요. Particles never stand alone.
tgt: 저는 밥을 먹어요: 저는 / 밥을 / 먹어요. Partikel tidak pernah berdiri sendiri.

src: Polite default greeting, any time of day.
tgt: Salam sopan sehari-hari, bisa dipakai jam berapa saja.
네 juga bisa berarti "oke" atau "iya, iya".

src: Point at the item and ask.
Ordering or shopping. 주세요 = please give.
tgt: Untuk memesan atau berbelanja. 주세요 = minta / tolong berikan.
Terima kasih, saya makan, ya (sebelum makan)

src: Lit. 'I will eat well.' Thanks to the cook.
tgt: Harfiah: "saya akan makan dengan baik". Terima kasih kepada yang memasak atau mentraktir.
Juga dipakai untuk menolak dengan sopan.
Dengan kalimat ini, orang jadi lebih sabar.

src: Squeezing past someone on the subway.
tgt: Untuk lewat di kereta bawah tanah yang penuh.

src: Look at the last Hangul block: 이에요 after a final consonant (저는 킴이에요), 예요 after a vowel (저는 리사예요).
tgt: Lihat blok Hangul terakhir: 이에요 setelah konsonan akhir (저는 킴이에요), 예요 setelah vokal (저는 리사예요).

src: Polite: 성함이 어떻게 되세요? for elders or formal settings.
tgt: Lebih sopan: 성함이 어떻게 되세요?, kepada orang yang lebih tua atau dalam situasi formal.

src: Lit. 'glad because we met'. Formal: 반갑습니다.
미국 = USA. 한국 Korea, 영국 UK, 캐나다 Canada, 멕시코 Mexico.
tgt: 미국 = Amerika Serikat. 한국 Korea, 영국 Inggris, 캐나다 Kanada, 멕시코 Meksiko.

src: Normal question in Korea; it decides how people speak to each other.
tgt: Pertanyaan biasa di Korea: jawabannya menentukan cara bicara, seperti kita memilih "Kak" atau "Dek".
Bilangan asli Korea + 살. 스물다섯 살 = 25 tahun.

src: 일 = work. 직업이 뭐예요? also works.
tgt: 일 = pekerjaan. 직업이 뭐예요? juga bisa.

src: 학생 student, 선생님 teacher, 개발자 developer, 간호사 nurse.
tgt: 학생 pelajar, 선생님 guru, 개발자 pengembang perangkat lunak, 간호사 perawat.

src: 공부하다 = to study. Say this and people light up.
tgt: 공부하다 = belajar. Ucapkan ini, dan lawan bicaramu akan senang sekali.

src: 취미 = hobby. 제 취미는 운동이에요 = my hobby is working out.
tgt: 취미 = hobi. 제 취미는 운동이에요 = hobi saya olahraga.

src: Said after introducing yourself at work or in a group. No English equivalent.
tgt: Diucapkan setelah memperkenalkan diri di tempat kerja atau dalam kelompok, seperti "mohon bimbingannya" kita.

src: Call a waiter or stop a stranger. Not an apology.
tgt: Untuk memanggil pelayan atau menghentikan orang di jalan, di saat kita bilang "Mas!" atau "Mbak!". Bukan permintaan maaf.

src: Same word as 'I'm fine' with rising tone.
tgt: Kata yang sama dengan "Tidak apa-apa", dengan nada naik.

src: Emergency or just a heavy bag.
tgt: Untuk keadaan darurat, atau sekadar tas yang berat.

src: Say it, then 다시 말해 주세요.
tgt: Ucapkan ini, lalu 다시 말해 주세요.
할 수 있다 = bisa. Berguna kalau bahasa Korea-mu belum cukup.

src: Point and ask. Works for food, signs, everything.
tgt: Tunjuk, lalu tanyakan. Bisa untuk makanan, papan tanda, apa saja.

src: I'm going to use the bathroom

tgt: 좀 melunakkan; 게요 memberi tahu apa yang akan kamu lakukan.

src: 돼요 = is it possible / does it work.

tgt: 배달 = pesan antar. Di Korea, apa saja bisa diantar.

src: 예약 = reservation. 예약 가능해요? = can I book?
tgt: 예약 = reservasi. 예약 가능해요? = bisa reservasi?

src: Shortest version of 천천히 말해 주세요.
tgt: Versi terpendek dari 천천히 말해 주세요.

src: Full form. Short: 화장실 어디예요? Both fine.
tgt: Bentuk lengkap. Singkatnya: 화장실 어디예요? Keduanya benar.

src: Cafés and small shops often don't have one inside.
tgt: Kafe dan toko kecil sering tidak punya toilet di dalam.

src: 아/어도 돼요 = is it okay if I…
Many café bathrooms have a keypad. It's printed on the receipt or ask staff.
tgt: Banyak toilet kafe memakai kunci angka. Kodenya tercetak di struk, atau tanyakan ke staf.

src: 휴지 = tissue/toilet paper. Carry some anyway.
tgt: 휴지 = tisu / tisu toilet. Sebaiknya tetap bawa sendiri.

src: GS25, CU, 세븐일레븐. There's always one.
tgt: GS25, CU, 세븐일레븐. Selalu ada yang dekat.
입구 = pintu masuk. 출구 = pintu keluar.

src: Subway exits are numbered. 3번 출구 = exit 3.
tgt: Pintu keluar stasiun kereta bawah tanah bernomor. 3번 출구 = pintu keluar 3.

src: Where is this? / Where am I?
tgt: Ini di mana? / Saya di mana?

src: 사다 = to buy. 팔아요? = do you sell it?
tgt: 사다 = membeli. 팔아요? = di sini menjual ini?

src: Is there a seat / a table?
Walking into a restaurant or café.
Answer to 몇 명이세요? (how many?). 한 명이요 = one. 세 명이요 = three.
tgt: Jawaban untuk 몇 명이세요? (berapa orang?). 한 명이요 = satu orang. 세 명이요 = tiga orang.

src: Cafés often lend them. 콘센트 = outlet.
tgt: Kafe sering meminjamkannya. 콘센트 = colokan listrik.

src: How long do I have to wait?
기다리다 = wait. 아/어야 돼요 = have to.
Could you take a photo for us?
Extra polite with 주실래요. Hand over the phone after.
tgt: 주실래요 membuatnya sangat sopan. Setelah itu, serahkan ponselmu.

src: 영수증 필요하세요? = do you need a receipt? (they'll ask).
tgt: 영수증 필요하세요? = perlu struk? (mereka akan menanyakannya).

src: Bags cost ~100원. 봉투 필요하세요? = need a bag?
tgt: Kantong plastik sekitar 100원. 봉투 필요하세요? = perlu kantong plastik?

src: 아아 (a-a) = iced Americano slang. 뜨아 = hot Americano.
tgt: 아아 (a-a) = singkatan gaul untuk es Americano. 뜨아 = Americano panas.

src: 따뜻한 = warm/hot. 차가운 거 = cold one.
tgt: 따뜻한 = hangat / panas. 차가운 거 = yang dingin.

src: Most cafés: 톨 / 그란데 / 벤티 or 레귤러 / 라지.
tgt: Di kebanyakan kafe: 톨 / 그란데 / 벤티 atau 레귤러 / 라지.

src: 큰 = big. 작은 거 = the small one.
tgt: 큰 = besar. 작은 거 = yang kecil.

src: 덜 = less. 안 달게 = not sweet.
tgt: 덜 = kurang. 안 달게 = tidak manis.

src: 빼다 = take out. 얼음 빼 주세요 = no ice.
tgt: 빼다 = mengeluarkan. 얼음 빼 주세요 = tolong tanpa es.

src: Answer: 네, 먹고 갈게요 (for here) / 포장이요 (to go).
tgt: Jawaban: 네, 먹고 갈게요 (makan di sini) / 포장이요 (dibawa pulang).

src: They hand you a pager; it buzzes when your order is ready.
tgt: Kamu diberi alat yang bergetar saat pesananmu siap.

src: Do you have a points card? (they ask)

tgt: Jawaban: 아니요, 괜찮아요 = tidak, terima kasih.

src: Convenience store cashiers ask this constantly.
Convenience store 도시락 and 삼각김밥. 데우다 = to heat.
tgt: Untuk 도시락 dan 삼각김밥 dari minimarket. 데우다 = memanaskan.

src: Self-serve heating area, usually by the window seats.
tgt: Tempat memanaskan sendiri, biasanya dekat kursi di sisi jendela.

src: For 컵라면 (cup noodles). It's free at every 편의점.
tgt: Untuk 컵라면 (mi gelas). Gratis di setiap 편의점.

src: Do you need a bag? (they ask)

tgt: Jawaban: 네 / 아니요. Kantong plastik sekitar 100원.

src: Is this buy one get one?
Korea's 1+1 / 2+1 stickers. Say 원 플러스 원.
tgt: Stiker 1+1 / 2+1 di Korea. Bacanya 원 플러스 원.

src: 현금으로 = by cash. Tap, no signature needed.
tgt: 현금으로 = dengan tunai. Cukup tempelkan kartu, tanpa tanda tangan.

src: 만 이천 → 만이천. Big numbers group by 만 (10,000).
tgt: 만 이천 → 만이천. Angka besar dikelompokkan per 만 (10.000), bukan per ribu seperti kita.

src: 삼만 팔천 구백. Say it slowly; cashiers show the screen anyway.
tgt: 삼만 팔천 구백. Ucapkan pelan-pelan; kasir biasanya juga menunjukkan layarnya.

src: Phone digits are Sino, and 0 is 공 (gong), not 영.
tgt: Angka nomor telepon memakai bilangan Sino-Korea, dan 0 dibaca 공 (gong), bukan 영.

src: 층 = floor, Sino number. 지하 1층 (B1) = jiha ilcheung.
tgt: 층 = lantai, dengan bilangan Sino-Korea. 지하 1층 (B1) = jiha ilcheung, basemen 1.

src: Hours are native: 두 시. 오후 = PM, 오전 = AM.
tgt: Jam memakai bilangan asli Korea: 두 시. 오후 = siang/sore, 오전 = pagi.
Jam dengan bilangan asli (아홉), menit dengan Sino-Korea (삼십).

src: Subway lines: 호선 with Sino numbers. 9호선 = guhoseon.
tgt: Jalur kereta bawah tanah: 호선 dengan bilangan Sino-Korea. 9호선 = guhoseon.

src: 번 = number. 몇 번 출구? = which exit?
tgt: 번 = nomor. 몇 번 출구? = pintu keluar nomor berapa?

src: 명 = person counter, native: 한 명, 두 명, 세 명, 네 명.
tgt: 명 = kata penggolong untuk orang, dengan bilangan asli: 한 명, 두 명, 세 명, 네 명.

src: 병 = bottle, native number. 잔 = glass.
tgt: 병 = botol, dengan bilangan asli. 잔 = gelas.

src: 개 = generic counter. 한 개, 두 개, 세 개, 네 개.
tgt: 개 = kata penggolong umum, seperti "buah" kita. 한 개, 두 개, 세 개, 네 개.

src: Months and days are Sino: 십일월 십삼일.
tgt: Bulan dan tanggal memakai bilangan Sino-Korea: 십일월 십삼일.

src: 퍼센트 from English. 반값 = half price.
tgt: 퍼센트 = persen, kata serapan. 반값 = setengah harga.

src: 개 = general things. 사과 한 개 = one apple.
tgt: 개 = untuk barang secara umum. 사과 한 개 = sebuah apel.

src: 명 = people. 분 is the polite version: 두 분.
tgt: 명 = orang. 분 adalah versi sopannya: 두 분.

src: 잔 = drinks in cups or glasses.
tgt: 잔 = minuman dalam gelas atau cangkir.

src: 병 = bottles. 소주 네 병 = four bottles of soju.
tgt: 병 = botol. 소주 네 병 = empat botol soju.

src: 마리 = animals. 고양이 다섯 마리 = five cats.
tgt: 마리 = hewan, seperti "ekor" kita. 고양이 다섯 마리 = lima ekor kucing.

src: 장 = flat things: paper, tickets, photos.
tgt: 장 = benda tipis dan datar: kertas, tiket, foto. Seperti "lembar" kita.

src: 시간 = hours of duration. 두 시 = 2 o'clock.
tgt: 시간 = jam sebagai lama waktu. 두 시 = jam dua.
번 = kali. Juga "nomor", untuk pintu keluar dan bus.

src: 달 = months (native). 일 개월 = one month (Sino, formal).
tgt: 달 = bulan (bilangan asli). 일 개월 = satu bulan (Sino-Korea, formal).

src: Special: 하루 (1 day), 이틀 (2), 사흘 (3). 일주일 = one week.
tgt: Bentuk khusus: 하루 (1 hari), 이틀 (2), 사흘 (3). 일주일 = satu minggu.

src: 몇 + counter = how many. Answer: 두 개요.
tgt: 몇 + kata penggolong = berapa. Jawaban: 두 개요.

src: 그릇 = bowls (rice, soup). 국밥 한 그릇 주세요.
tgt: 그릇 = mangkuk (nasi, sup). 국밥 한 그릇 주세요.

src: 봉지 = bag/packet of snacks or chips.
날씨 = weather. 어때요 = how is it.
Summer in Seoul: 덥고 습해요 = hot and humid.
tgt: Musim panas di Seoul: 덥고 습해요 = panas dan lembap.

src: 겨울 = winter. 너무 추워요 = so cold.
tgt: 겨울 = musim dingin. 너무 추워요 = dingin sekali.

src: 비 = rain. 우산 있어요? = do you have an umbrella?
tgt: 비 = hujan. 우산 있어요? = bawa payung?

src: 눈 = snow (also eye). 첫눈 = first snow, a date thing in Korea.
tgt: 눈 = salju (juga "mata"). 첫눈 = salju pertama, momen romantis di Korea.

src: Check the 미세먼지 level daily; people mask up when it's 나쁨.
tgt: Cek kadar 미세먼지 setiap hari; kalau 나쁨 (buruk), orang memakai masker.

src: 기분 = mood. 기분이 안 좋아요 = I feel bad.
tgt: 기분 = suasana hati. 기분이 안 좋아요 = suasana hati saya buruk.
Kata perasaan yang paling sering dipakai di Korea.

src: 긴장 = tension. Before a test or a date.
tgt: 긴장 = ketegangan. Sebelum ujian atau kencan.

src: 화 = anger. 화내지 마 = don't be mad.
tgt: 화 = amarah. 화내지 마 = jangan marah.

src: 놀라다. 깜짝 놀랐어요 = you startled me.
tgt: 놀라다. 깜짝 놀랐어요 = saya kaget sekali.

src: Polite version. Casual 보고 싶어 is in Sweet talk.
tgt: Versi sopan. Versi santai, 보고 싶어, ada di dek Kata-kata manis.

src: 설레다 = the butterflies feeling. Very K-drama.
tgt: 설레다 = deg-degan karena senang. Sangat drakor.
짜증 = rasa kesal. 짜증 나! bentuk santai.

src: Joins sentences. 밥 먹었어요. 그리고 커피 마셨어요.
tgt: Menyambung kalimat. 밥 먹었어요. 그리고 커피 마셨어요.

src: Soft contrast or topic shift. Casual: 근데.
tgt: Pertentangan halus atau ganti topik. Santai: 근데.

src: 먼저 손 씻어요 = wash hands first.
tgt: 먼저 손 씻어요 = cuci tangan dulu.

src: 커피 아니면 차? = coffee or tea?
tgt: 커피 아니면 차? = kopi atau teh?

src: 그럼 내일 봐요 = then see you tomorrow.
tgt: 그럼 내일 봐요 = kalau begitu, sampai besok.

src: Green cross sign. Many open late; 편의점 sells basics.
tgt: Cari tanda salib hijau. Banyak yang buka sampai malam; 편의점 menjual obat-obat dasar.

src: 아프다 = to hurt. 배가 아파요 = stomachache.
tgt: 아프다 = sakit. 배가 아파요 = perut saya sakit.

src: 열 = fever. 열 나요 also works.
tgt: 열 = demam. 열 나요 juga bisa.

src: 땅콩 알레르기 = peanut allergy. Say it before ordering too.
tgt: 땅콩 알레르기 = alergi kacang tanah. Sampaikan juga sebelum memesan makanan.

src: Pharmacies next to clinics fill them in minutes.
tgt: Apotek di samping klinik menyiapkannya dalam beberapa menit.

src: How many times a day do I take it?
식후 30분 = 30 min after meals, the usual answer.
tgt: 식후 30분 = 30 menit setelah makan, jawaban yang biasa.

src: I need to go to the hospital
아/어야 돼요 = have to. 응급실 = ER.
여행자 보험 = travel insurance. 영수증 for claims.
tgt: 여행자 보험 = asuransi perjalanan. Simpan 영수증 untuk klaim.

src: Point. 많이 아파요 = it hurts a lot.
tgt: Tunjuk bagiannya. 많이 아파요 = sakit sekali.

src: Said by doctors and friends alike.
Sold at every 편의점 and 약국.
tgt: Dijual di setiap 편의점 dan 약국.

src: After too much 삼겹살. 까스활명수 is the classic.
tgt: Setelah kebanyakan makan 삼겹살. 까스활명수 obat klasiknya.

src: One-room. 투룸 = two rooms. 오피스텔 = officetel.
tgt: Satu ruangan. 투룸 = dua kamar. 오피스텔 = officetel (kantor sekaligus hunian).

src: Can be huge in Korea. 전세 = deposit-only lease.
tgt: Di Korea jumlahnya bisa sangat besar. 전세 = sewa hanya dengan uang jaminan besar.

src: 월세 얼마예요? = how much is rent?
tgt: 월세 얼마예요? = sewanya berapa per bulan?
관리비 = iuran pengelolaan gedung. 포함 = termasuk.

src: 택배 = parcel delivery. 문 앞에 놔 주세요 = leave it at the door.
tgt: 택배 = jasa kirim paket. 문 앞에 놔 주세요 = tolong taruh di depan pintu.

src: Strict: 플라스틱 / 종이 / 캔 / 음식물. Fines exist.
tgt: Aturannya ketat: 플라스틱 / 종이 / 캔 / 음식물. Ada dendanya.

src: Needs its own bag or card-based bin.
tgt: Harus pakai kantong khusus atau tempat sampah yang dibuka dengan kartu.

src: Buy at 편의점; must use it for general trash.
tgt: Dibeli di 편의점; wajib untuk sampah umum.
코인 세탁 = laundry koin, buka 24 jam.

src: Please tell me the door code
Most doors use keypads, not keys.
tgt: Kebanyakan pintu memakai kunci angka, bukan anak kunci.

src: 부동산 = real-estate office, where you find rooms.
tgt: 부동산 = kantor agen properti, tempat mencari kamar.

src: I send parcels from the convenience store
GS25/CU have parcel counters. Cheap and easy.
tgt: GS25 dan CU punya layanan kirim paket. Murah dan mudah.

src: 드시다 = honorific of 먹다/마시다. 맛있게 드세요 = enjoy your meal.
tgt: 드시다 = bentuk hormat dari 먹다/마시다. 맛있게 드세요 = selamat makan.

src: 주무시다 = honorific of 자다. 안녕히 주무세요 = good night (polite).
tgt: 주무시다 = bentuk hormat dari 자다. 안녕히 주무세요 = selamat tidur (sopan).

src: 계시다 = honorific of 있다 (for people). 안녕히 계세요.
tgt: 계시다 = bentuk hormat dari 있다 (untuk orang). 안녕히 계세요.

src: 말씀 = honorific of 말. 말씀해 주세요 = please tell me.
tgt: 말씀 = bentuk hormat dari 말. 말씀해 주세요 = tolong katakan.

src: 연세 = honorific of 나이. For elders.
tgt: 연세 = bentuk hormat dari 나이. Untuk orang yang lebih tua.

src: 가다 + 시 + 어요 → 가세요. 조심히 가세요.
tgt: 가다 + 시 + 어요 → 가세요. 조심히 가세요.

src: 오다 + 시 + 었어요 → 오셨어요. 언제 오셨어요?
tgt: 오다 + 시 + 었어요 → 오셨어요. 언제 오셨어요?

src: 안녕하세요 is literally 'are you at peace' with 시.
tgt: 안녕하세요 secara harfiah berarti "apakah Anda dalam keadaan damai", dengan 시.

src: 님 raises 아버지/어머니. For your partner's parents.
tgt: 님 meninggikan 아버지/어머니. Untuk orang tua pasanganmu.

src: Someone else's grandmother, or very formal speech. Elderly strangers: 할머니 or 어르신.
tgt: Nenek orang lain, atau dalam bahasa yang sangat formal. Untuk nenek yang tidak dikenal: 할머니 atau 어르신.
식사 = "makan", agak hormat. 하셨어요 = sudah melakukan (hormat).

src: 카페 is far more common in speech.
Health + 장 (place). 헬스하다 = to work out.
Also used for any doctor's clinic.
Look for the green cross sign.
모텔 is cheaper; 게스트하우스 for backpackers.
책 읽는 거 좋아해요 is more natural in speech.
여행 가요 = I go on a trip.
음악 들어요 = I listen to music.
-기 turns a verb into a noun.
게임해요 = I play games. PC방 = internet café.
National pastime — expect full gear on easy trails.
Comes free with almost every meal.
Three-layer meat. Wrap it in lettuce: 쌈.
Refills are free: 반찬 좀 더 주세요.
사과 apple, 딸기 strawberry, 귤 tangerine.
빙수 = shaved ice; 호떡 = sweet pancake.
녹차 green, 보리차 barley, 유자차 citron.
사이다 is Sprite-style, not alcoholic cider.
Ask for 물 at restaurants — it's free.
생맥주 = draft beer. 카스, 테라, 클라우드.
Goes with 파전 on rainy days.
얼음 빼 주세요 = no ice please.
잔 is the counter for glasses/cups.
짠! among friends; 건배 at dinners.
쉬다. 주말에 쉬어요 = I rest on weekends.
놀다. 같이 놀자 = let's hang out.
K-drama = 한국 드라마 or just 드라마.
런닝맨, 유 퀴즈 — unscripted comedy shows.
영화 보러 갈래? = wanna go see a movie?
Many dramas are based on 웹툰.
화 is the counter for episodes. 3화 = episode 3.
본방송 = original airing; 본방사수 = watch it live.
건물 앞에서 만나요 = meet in front of the building.
은행 옆에 있어요 = it's next to the bank.
카페와 약국 사이에 = between the café and pharmacy.
여기서 가까워요? = Is it close from here?
코너에서 왼쪽으로 = left at the corner.
신호등에서 우회전 = turn right at the light.
Shorter than 똑바로 가세요; seen on signs.
이에요 after consonant, 예요 after vowel: 학생이에요, 저예요.
Past: 갔어요. 집에 가요 = I'm going home.
Past: 먹었어요. 밥 먹었어요? = Did you eat?
Past: 봤어요. 내일 봐요 = see you tomorrow.
좋아요 = it's good / I like it (adjective form).
Verb stem + 아/어 주세요 = please do X.
은 after consonant, 는 after vowel. 저는 = as for me.
이 after consonant, 가 after vowel. 비가 와요 = rain is falling.
을 after consonant, 를 after vowel. 밥을 먹어요.
학교에 가요 = go to school. 세 시에 = at 3 o'clock.
at / in (where an action happens), from
Often pronounced 에. 친구의 책 = friend's book.
하고 is the safe spoken choice.
Native numbers: age, counting things, hours.
Before a counter, 하나→한, 둘→두, 셋→세, 넷→네.
Sino numbers: money, dates, minutes, phone numbers.
Korean counts in 만 (10k). 오만 원 = 50,000 won.
Also for things: a pretty café.
Casual. Polite: 잘 자요; to elders: 안녕히 주무세요.
How Koreans say 'how are you' to people they care about.
네요 = noticing out loud. Casual: 오늘 예쁘네.
눈 = eyes. 웃는 모습이 예뻐요 = your smile is pretty.
The way you laugh is so cute
Casual: 보고 싶었어. Say it on arrival.
I'm happy when I'm with you
같이 = together. 행복하다 = to be happy.
I thought about you a lot
Did you eat? Make sure you eat well
Peak Korean affection: caring about meals.
Text this after a date. Expected, not optional.
Lit. 'dream a good dream'. Pairs with 잘 자.
You're the only one for me
Casual, playful way to ask someone out.
Do you want to go out with me?
사귀다 = to date. The real ask.
Stop being cute, my heart hurts
좀 softens it. Polite: 번호 좀 알려 주실래요?
The modern number ask. 인스타 = Insta.
If you're free, want to grab a coffee?
여자친구 = girlfriend. 남친/여친 = casual short forms.
It was love at first sight
첫눈 = first sight (also first snow). 반하다 = fall for.
Time flies when I'm with you
Thinking of you makes me smile
웃음이 나다 = a smile comes out.
제일 = the most. 제일 멋있어 for guys.
ㄹ게 = I'll (promise). Classic end of date.
것 같아 = I think / it seems. Softens the confession.
I don't want to go home tonight
기 싫다 = don't want to. Said at the end of a good date.
자 = let's. More confident than 사귈래?
The universal opener. Polite: 뭐 해요?
심심하다 = bored. 놀자 = let's hang out.
Lit. 'I go now'. 다 왔어 = I'm almost there.
것 같아 = I think. 미안, 늦었어 = sorry I'm late.
Texting only. ㅎㅎ = softer chuckle. ㅠㅠ = crying.
Texting shorthand for 응. ㄴㄴ = no.
Casual 몰라요. 글쎄 = hmm, not sure.
Also 'is that so?' with rising tone.
Works for people, outfits, moves. Polite: 멋있어요.
짱 = top. 짱 멋있어 = super cool.
Said about a goal, a beat, a view. Casual.
Safe hype word for any crowd.
End-of-day sign-off at work or practice.
지 마 = don't. 걱정하지 마 full form.
한잔 = one glass. The friend-making phrase.
Close friends / same age only. To anyone older it's rude.
놀다 = to play / hang out. 자 = let's.
Lit. 'come out'. 빨리 나와 = hurry up and come out.
돼 = is it possible / does it work.
으러 가다 = go in order to. 커피 마시러 갈래? = wanna go get coffee?
보다 → 볼래. 게임 할래? = wanna play games?
Shall we go to a café?
ㄹ까 = shall we? Softer than ㄹ래.
우리 집 = my (our) house. Koreans say 우리 for their own home.
ㄹ게 = I'll. 금방 갈게 = I'll be there soon.
